title: Representing finite traces preserve the actual quotient counits
statement: Let A and B be finite commutative rings, N,M positive integers with N=0 in A and M=0 in B, and φ:A→B a ring homomorphism. Let f:X→Y be a quasi-compact separated compactifiable morphism of Noetherian schemes and d a nonnegative integer. Let a and b be normalized SmoothLevel data over A and B, and let r be ReductionData between them [def-pur-finite-smooth-adjunction-data], with the actual maps of [def-pur-finite-smooth-canonical-maps] and [def-pur-finite-smooth-coefficient-arrows]. First, for every ordinary bounded constructible finite-Tor K on Y and every ordinary derived test Q on X, v↦Rf_!(v)≫trace_A(K) is a bijection from Hom(Q,f_A^*K(d)[2d]) to Hom(Rf_!Q,K). Second, write S_X,S_Y for scalar extension, F_B for pro-etale compact support over B, γ_A and γ_B for the two pro-etale purity maps, λ for r's purity-source comparison, c for its exceptional coefficient map, b^{-1} for the actual inverse compact-support coefficient comparison on the exceptional value, and ε_A for the actual pro-etale exceptional counit. For every pro-etale constructible finite-Tor K on Y, the following equality of actual arrows holds: F_B(S_X(γ_A(K)))≫b^{-1}≫S_Y(ε_A(K)) = F_B(λ_K)≫trace_B(S_Y K). In particular this is an equality of counits, not just an isomorphism of their source objects.

proof.text: SmoothLevel.ordinary_isIso makes the specified gamma invertible. Its actual counit transpose is the definition of trace. Apply the generic representing-trace theorem to this isomorphism and the ordinary exceptional adjunction.

The pro_counit field gives F_B(c_K)≫ε_B=b^{-1}≫S_Y(ε_A). Substitute this equation into the left side. Functoriality combines the two F_B factors. The pro_purity field identifies S_X(γ_A)≫c_K with λ_K≫γ_B. Expand functoriality and the definition of proTrace to obtain the right side.

    {A : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    {N : ℕ} {hN : 0 < N} {hA : (N : A) = 0}
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [HasCompactification f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsSeparated f] (d : ℕ)
    (s : SmoothLevel A N hN hA f d) (K : DerivedCategoryModule A Y)

    (Q : DerivedCategoryModule A X) :
    Function.Bijective (fun a : Q ⟶ (puritySource A f (line A N hA X d)).obj K ↦
      (rightDerivedLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f).map a ≫

theorem finiteTrace_quotient_counit
    {A B : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] [Finite A] [CommRing B] [Finite B]
    {phi : A →+* B} {N M : ℕ} {hN : 0 < N} {hM : 0 < M}
    {hA : (N : A) = 0} {hB : (M : B) = 0}
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [HasCompactification f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsSeparated f] (d : ℕ)
    {a : SmoothLevel A N hN hA f d} {b : SmoothLevel B M hM hB f d}
    (r : ReductionData phi f d a b) (K : proCategory A Y) (hK : IsCtf A Y K) :
    (proCompact B f).map
        ((proScalar phi X).map (proGamma A f (line A N hA X d) a.alpha K)) ≫
      proCompactCoefficientInverse phi f ((exceptional A f).obj K) ≫
        (proScalar phi Y).map (proCounit A f K) =
    (proCompact B f).map (proLambda f d r.twist K) ≫
      proTrace B f (line B M hB X d) b.alpha ((proScalar phi Y).obj K)
